claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure containing dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and exhibits brittle failure.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations in the untreated alloy.
Local stress concentrations associated with dislocation pile-ups trigger microcracking and brittle failure.
The proposed intervention is approximately 1 at% Nb microalloying followed by homogenization annealing.
Homogenization annealing after Nb addition will promote Nb segregation at lamellar interfaces.
The treatment will produce Nb-enriched lamellar boundaries.
Nb segregation at internal lamellar boundaries lowers the barrier to dislocation transfer across phases.
Easier dislocation transfer across phases reduces dislocation pile-up accumulation.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups reduces local stress concentrations and microcracking during tensile straining.
The Nb and annealing treatment will significantly improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
Uniform elongation may increase by approximately two- to threefold relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will preserve or modestly increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
The proposed improvements apply under room-temperature tensile loading.
The treatment's effectiveness depends on Nb content and annealing parameters being sufficient for segregation without deleteriously changing the lamellar structure.
Excessive segregation could cause secondary-phase formation or over-softening.
